title: Adaptation of Generalist Robot Policies with Minimal Data
abstract: arXiv:2608.11363v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A central goal in robot learning is to move beyond task-specific human data collection toward robots that improve through autonomous interaction. Yet fully autonomous learning remains difficult with current policies: sparse rewards and weak zero-shot exploration make it unlikely that a robot will discover successful behavior from scratch. We study minimal-data adaptation, a regime in which a pre-trained robot policy must learn a new task from as little as one demonstration followed by autonomous online interaction. This setting serves as the closest tractable proxy for fully autonomous improvement, allowing us to study whether minimal human guidance can bootstrap autonomous learning and what algorithmic ingredients make it feasible. We build MiDAS, a simple offline-to-online RL recipe that first anchors a pre-trained VLA to the target task with behavior cloning on single/few demonstrations, then improves it through value-based online R

translated_title: 基于最小数据适应通用机器人策略
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.11363v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：机器人学习的一个核心目标是超越针对特定任务的人工数据收集，转向通过自主交互来改进的机器人。然而，在当前策略下，完全自主的学习仍然困难：稀疏奖励和弱的零样本探索使得机器人不太可能从零开始发现成功行为。我们研究了最小数据适应，这是一种预训练机器人策略必须从尽可能少的一个演示开始，随后进行自主在线交互来学习新任务的机制。这一设置作为完全自主改进的最接近可行代理，使我们能够研究最小人工指导是否能启动自主学习，以及哪些算法成分使其可行。我们构建了MiDAS，一个简单的离线到在线强化学习配方，首先通过单次或少量演示的行为克隆将预训练的VLA锚定到目标任务，然后通过基于价值的在线强化学习进行改进。
tldr: 本文提出了MiDAS方法，通过最小数据（单次或少量演示）结合离线到在线强化学习，使预训练机器人策略能高效适应新任务，验证了最小人工指导可启动自主学习的可行性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes MiDAS, a minimal-data adaptation method combining behavior cloning on single/few demonstrations with offline-to-online RL, enabling pre-trained robot policies to efficiently adapt to new tasks and demonstrating that minimal human guidance can bootstrap autonomous learning.
